title: Practical Low-Weight Codes For Energy-Efficient Bus Encoding
authors: Marco Chiani Lorenzo Valentini
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the transmission of data encoded into binary messages, with the goal of minimizing the Hamming distance, i.e., the number of bit-flips, between consecutive messages. This problem is relevant for enhancing the longevity of Non-Volatile Memories and reducing transition-induced energy consumption in data buses. Known as Write-Efficient Memory coding in the literature, this challenge has traditionally been addressed using optimal but complex schemes. In low-power computer systems the same topic is known as bus encoding. In this paper, we derive closed-form expressions to evaluate the average number of bit-flips for practical, sub-optimal encoding schemes, and propose two new schemes assisted by predefined random codebooks. We demonstrate that low-complexity solutions achieve performance very close to the optimal schemes, making them attractive for implementation in energy-sensitive and memory-critical applications. For instance, by adding 8 extra bits to 64-bits data, sub-optimal schemes can achieve a bit-flip reduction (related to energy saving) of approximately 24.7%, compared to the 26.4% reduction offered by the significantly more complex optimal scheme.
tldr: This paper proposes low-complexity encoding schemes to minimize bit-flips in data buses for energy efficiency, targeting non-volatile memories and low-power systems.
motivation: Reducing bit-flips in data transmission can extend memory longevity and lower energy consumption in data buses, but optimal schemes are complex; practical sub-optimal solutions are needed.
method: The authors derive closed-form expressions for average bit-flips in sub-optimal encodings and propose two new schemes using predefined random codebooks.
result: With 8 extra bits on 64-bit data, sub-optimal schemes achieve ~24.7% bit-flip reduction versus 26.4% for optimal schemes, showing near-optimal performance at lower complexity.
conclusion: Low-complexity encoding schemes can achieve energy savings close to optimal, making them attractive for energy-sensitive and memory-critical applications.

title: Block Tensor Rank Of Sum-Rank Metric Codes
authors: Huimin Lao, Huy Pham, Hoang Ta, van Khu Vu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sum-rank codes provide a generalized framework for Hamming and rank-metric codes, with codewords represented as tuples of matrices and weight given by the sum of the block ranks. In this paper, we introduce and study a block-tensor-rank invariant for sum-rank metric codes. To each code, we associate its : the smallest number of block-simple tensors, namely rank-one matrices supported inside single blocks, whose linear span contains the code. In general, determining the block tensor rank of a sum-rank code is challenging. Our main structural result shows that the block tensor rank decomposes additively across the blocks of the code, thereby reducing its computation to a tensor-rank problem on each block projection. Consequently, we derive two complementary lower bounds on the block tensor rank, referred to as the and the . Moreover, by combining the coordinate-code bound with the classical Singleton and Griesmer bounds for codes in the Hamming metric, we obtain explicit lower bounds, called the and the , respectively. We further construct families of sum-rank codes whose block tensor ranks attain the Singleton or Griesmer coordinate-code bounds. These constructions are based on Hamming-metric codes achieving the corresponding classical bounds. Finally, we show that, in certain cases, the block tensor ranks of two known families of sum-rank codes in the literature do not attain the Singleton coordinate-code bound.
tldr: This paper introduces a block tensor rank invariant for sum-rank metric codes and derives bounds based on classical coding theory.
motivation: Sum-rank codes generalize Hamming and rank-metric codes, and understanding their structure is important for coding theory.
method: The authors define block tensor rank, show it decomposes additively across blocks, and derive lower bounds using coordinate-code and classical Singleton/Griesmer bounds.
result: They obtain explicit lower bounds (Singleton and Griesmer coordinate-code bounds) and construct families of codes attaining these bounds.
conclusion: The block tensor rank provides a new invariant for sum-rank codes, with connections to classical coding bounds.

title: A New Class Of Efficient Linear Higher-order Schemes For The Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert Equation With Reduced Restriction On The Damping Parameter
authors: Fukeng Huang, Binghong Li, Xiaoli Li, Jie Shen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical high-order backward differentiation formula (BDF) methods for the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation often suffer from restrictive stability constraints, requiring small time steps and imposing stringent lower bounds on the damping parameter. These limitations become particularly severe for schemes of order higher than three. In this paper, we develop a class of high-order generalized BDF (GBDF) schemes for the LLG equation, including both semi-implicit and fully explicit treatments of the gyromagnetic term. The proposed schemes significantly improve stability properties and substantially relax the damping parameter constraints, but introduce essential difficulty in its analysis compared to the classical BDF schemes. We construct a novel multiplier which enables us to carry out a energy-based error analysis. This approach yields optimal-order error estimates under considerably weaker assumptions on the damping parameter than those required for classical BDF schemes. Numerical experiments are presented to confirm the theoretical results, and demonstrate that the proposed GBDF schemes achieve higher accuracy, enhanced stability, and much wider admissible damping regimes compared to classical high-order BDF methods.
tldr: This paper develops high-order numerical schemes for the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, focusing on stability and damping parameter constraints.
motivation: Classical high-order BDF methods for the LLG equation suffer from restrictive stability constraints and require small time steps, especially for higher orders. The authors aim to develop schemes with improved stability and relaxed damping parameter bounds.
method: The authors propose a class of generalized BDF (GBDF) schemes, including semi-implicit and fully explicit treatments of the gyromagnetic term. They construct a novel multiplier to enable energy-based error analysis.
result: Optimal-order error estimates are obtained under weaker assumptions on the damping parameter than classical BDF schemes. Numerical experiments confirm higher accuracy, enhanced stability, and wider admissible damping regimes.
conclusion: The proposed GBDF schemes significantly improve upon classical high-order BDF methods for the LLG equation, offering better stability and broader applicability.

title: Dynamical Cantor Staircase Functions And The Small Flow Boundary Property
authors: Tomasz Downarowicz, Yonatan Gutman, Chunlin Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14337v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The small flow boundary property (SFBP), introduced by Burguet for fixed-point free topological flows, is a non-trivial generalization of the small boundary property (SBP). We characterize when a time-discretization of such a flow satisfies the SBP and deduce that an SFBP flow admitting an aperiodic time-discretization has vanishing mean dimension. Furthermore, we introduce a new quantity, , for a factor between a flow and a time-discretization, quantifying the dynamical complexity inherited from the flow itself. This is used in order to establish that any time-discretization of a flow with SFBP admits factors of arbitrarily small flow-generated entropy separating any fixed pair of distinct points. The argument relies on a construction of a dynamical version of the Cantor staircase function. Finally, the appendix includes proofs of fundamental properties of the marker property which have not yet appeared in the literature.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical Cantor staircase functions and the small flow boundary property in topological dynamics, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To characterize the small flow boundary property for topological flows and relate it to mean dimension and entropy.
method: Uses time-discretization, marker properties, and construction of dynamical Cantor staircase functions.
result: Shows that an SFBP flow with an aperiodic time-discretization has vanishing mean dimension, and that any time-discretization of an SFBP flow admits factors with arbitrarily small flow-generated entropy separating points.
conclusion: The small flow boundary property imposes strong constraints on the complexity of flows and their discretizations.

title: Noncoherent Isac Over Block-Fading Channels: Asymptotic Performance Analysis
authors: Hao Yang, Kai Wan, Giuseppe Caire
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the fundamental limits and optimal signal distribution design for Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems operating under strictly noncoherent conditions. Unlike conventional coherent frameworks that rely on perfect channel state information, we consider a block-fading MIMO channel where the channel realizations are unknown to both the transmitter and the receiver. We adopt a realization-wise perspective to characterize the noncoherent performance tradeoff across different signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regimes. In the high-SNR regime, we derive a lower bound for the noncoherent mutual information and define a metric, termed sensing-induced rate loss, to quantify the communication penalty incurred by sensing-oriented beamforming. We then employ a projected gradient algorithm to optimize the spatial power allocation, balancing the conflict between the unitary space-time modulation-based structure for communication and the task-oriented spatial power allocation for sensing. Conversely, in the low-SNR regime, we perform a first-order asymptotic analysis of the ergodic minimum mean squared error (EMMSE). Our theoretical derivation reveals a fundamental synergy: the sensing-optimal strategy collapses to a rank-one transmission along the dominant eigenvector of the target response, which incurs no first-order communication loss in the low-SNR regime. This result demonstrates that the conflicting tradeoff observed at high SNR vanishes asymptotically at low SNR, enabling perfect alignment between sensing and communication objectives.
tldr: This paper analyzes the fundamental limits of noncoherent integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) over block-fading MIMO channels, focusing on asymptotic performance in high and low SNR regimes.
motivation: Conventional ISAC systems assume perfect channel knowledge, but in practice, channel state information may be unavailable. The authors aim to characterize the tradeoff between sensing and communication under strictly noncoherent conditions.
method: The authors derive lower bounds on noncoherent mutual information and define a sensing-induced rate loss metric. They use a projected gradient algorithm for spatial power allocation and perform first-order asymptotic analysis of ergodic minimum mean squared error (EMMSE) in the low-SNR regime.
result: In the high-SNR regime, sensing-oriented beamforming incurs a communication penalty quantified by the sensing-induced rate loss. In the low-SNR regime, the sensing-optimal strategy is rank-one transmission along the dominant target eigenvector, causing no first-order communication loss.
conclusion: The conflicting tradeoff between sensing and communication at high SNR vanishes asymptotically at low SNR, enabling perfect alignment of objectives.

title: The Program Is Still There: A Conservation Law For Program Discovery
authors: Jorge Miguel Silva
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finding the shortest program that generates a sequence is uncomputable, and for six decades that fact has been mistaken for a wall around finding any generating program. It is not a wall but a price, and this paper measures it. For every algorithm that learns about a candidate program only through its score, a class spanning Levin search, evolutionary methods, simulated annealing, and the cross-entropy method, we define the coupling width of a search problem and prove an unconditional worst-case lower bound, exponential in that width with base one less than the domain size. From it follows a conservation law: structural knowledge injected into a search trades one for one against the search it removes, and their sum can never fall below the length of the program sought. Levin's 1973 upper bound and the lower bound proved here are the two ends of one conserved quantity, closing on each other as the instruction set grows. The only escape is to read a candidate's structure rather than its score, and its price, which we prove for generic targets, is incompleteness. A deterministic engine built on this theory recovers a generating program, certified by compressing its data and predicting an unseen continuation, for 2,383 of 3,914 sequences across four independent populations, including 244 of the 256 elementary cellular automata, with measured discovery cost rising along program length more than an order of magnitude inside the score-oracle worst case.
tldr: The paper proves a conservation law for program discovery via score-based search, showing that structural knowledge trades off against search effort.
motivation: The uncomputability of finding the shortest program has been misinterpreted as an impossibility; the author aims to quantify the cost of program discovery.
method: Defines coupling width and proves an unconditional worst-case lower bound for any algorithm that learns only through a score function, then derives a conservation law linking injected knowledge to search removed.
result: A lower bound exponential in coupling width is proven, and a deterministic engine recovers generating programs for 2,383 out of 3,914 sequences, including 244 elementary cellular automata.
conclusion: Score-based program discovery has a fundamental trade-off between structural knowledge and search effort, with the only escape being direct structure reading at the cost of incompleteness.

title: Choric Masking In Ambient Release Systems: A Finite Certificate Calculus For Trace Indistinguishability Under Bounded Audiences
authors: Taylan Alpay Faruk Alpay
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a finite certificate calculus for ambient release systems, staged probabilistic environments in which a protected coordinate is not observed directly but can remain statistically readable through visible roles, timing, repeated movement, bounded attention, linked rooms, and post-release state. The security notion, choric masking, requires the trace law induced by a protected locus to lie inside or near the convex hull of admissible cover traces under the tests available to a specified audience. For finite horizons, trace laws form polytopes, audiences induce measurement operators, and masking becomes intersection in the projected measurement space. Exposure is certified by separating hyperplanes, kernel obstructions, hypothesis-testing bounds, Fano-type localization lower bounds, and support separation in downstream rooms. The calculus distinguishes trace residue from carrier localization, full-trace exposure from attention-filtered exposure, first-room masking from delayed post-release exposure, and unresolved system pressure from carrier hazard. It proves measurement-polytope equivalence for exact and approximate masks, dual separation certificates, data-processing laws for attention lenses, aperture identities for gaze-thinned observation, lower bounds for mandatory unique gestures, composition rules for linked releases, and a repeated-room debt theorem showing how unresolved pressure can broaden selection and shift cost onto cover populations without localizing the source. The result is a finite, checkable language for auditing privacy, unlinkability, side-channel leakage, and accountability in public-facing release systems.
tldr: This paper develops a finite certificate calculus for privacy analysis in ambient release systems using trace indistinguishability under bounded audiences.
motivation: To provide a formal framework for auditing privacy, unlinkability, and side-channel leakage in public-facing systems where sensitive coordinates are not directly observed.
method: It models trace laws as polytopes, audiences as measurement operators, and masking as intersection in projected measurement space, using separating hyperplanes and information-theoretic bounds.
result: It proves measurement-polytope equivalence, dual separation certificates, data-processing laws for attention lenses, and a repeated-room debt theorem.
conclusion: The calculus offers a finite, checkable language for privacy auditing, but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Pseudonym Scheme Based On Hybrid Certificates For Security Credential Management System In Vehicular Communications
authors: Abel C. H. Chen, F. J. Hwang, Yu-Chih Wei, Chin-Chen Chang, Bon-Yeh Lin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent years, the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) and the European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI) have developed a series of security communication standards for vehicular communications. These standards include mechanisms such as the Security Credential Management System (SCMS) and Butterfly Key Expansion (BKE) to protect vehicle privacy. However, these standards are mainly based on the Elliptic-Curve Cryptography (ECC), which may be vulnerable to attacks from quantum computing in the future. In response to this potential risk, this study proposes a hybrid certificate that combines the ECC with Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC). This approach enables infrastructure systems to be built on cryptographic foundations that are more resilient to quantum-based attacks. Furthermore, this study presents a generalized pseudonym scheme that is compatible with various cryptographic algorithms for generating pseudonym certificates. This design aims to eliminate the possibility of inferring any correlation between the public key in a pseudonym certificate and that in an enrollment certificate. This study also conducts a comprehensive performance evaluation of the RSA, ECC, and PQC algorithms, particularly those standardized by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). The comparison considers factors such as message length and computation time. Based on the findings, this study recommends suitable pseudonym schemes that adopt hybrid certificates for secure and efficient use in vehicular communications.
tldr: This paper proposes a hybrid certificate scheme combining ECC and post-quantum cryptography for vehicular communication security, focusing on pseudonym generation and performance evaluation.
motivation: Current vehicular security standards based on ECC may be vulnerable to future quantum attacks, so a hybrid approach with PQC is proposed to enhance resilience.
method: The authors design a hybrid certificate that integrates ECC with NIST-standardized PQC algorithms, and develop a generalized pseudonym scheme compatible with various cryptographic algorithms. Performance is evaluated in terms of message length and computation time.
result: The hybrid certificate scheme provides quantum-resistant security while maintaining practical efficiency, with recommendations for suitable pseudonym schemes based on performance trade-offs.
conclusion: The proposed hybrid certificate and pseudonym scheme offer a viable path to quantum-safe vehicular communications, balancing security and performance.

title: Securing The Future Of IoMT In The Post-Quantum Era: An Edge-Native Federated Learning Approach
authors: Taym Alshoghri, Deemah H. Tashman, Mohammad Reza Gerami, Soumaya Cherkaoui
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices operate under strict resource constraints while handling highly sensitive health data, making security and privacy critical concerns. Federated learning (FL) further complicates this landscape, as model updates exchanged during training may unintentionally expose private medical information. Emerging quantum computing capabilities threaten the long-term viability of conventional lightweight cryptographic mechanisms, motivating the integration of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) into IoMT systems. This article discusses key enabling technologies for quantum-resilient IoMT, including post-quantum key establishment, lightweight encryption, and edge-native orchestration. We propose a scalable Kubernetes-based framework that integrates PQC into FL-enabled IoMT environments and validate it on a Raspberry Pi testbed. Results demonstrate that distributed cryptographic processing significantly reduces latency compared to sequential designs while maintaining feasible resource overhead. The primary contribution of this work lies in the design and validation of a secure orchestration and communication framework for FL-enabled IoMT systems. We conclude by outlining future directions toward energy-aware architectures, intelligent security optimization, and resilient next-generation Intelligent Internet of Medical Things (IIoMT) ecosystems.
tldr: This paper proposes a Kubernetes-based framework integrating post-quantum cryptography into federated learning for IoMT devices, focusing on practical security and latency optimization.
motivation: IoMT devices are resource-constrained and handle sensitive health data, and emerging quantum computers threaten current cryptographic mechanisms, necessitating quantum-resilient solutions.
method: The authors design a scalable orchestration framework using Kubernetes and post-quantum key establishment, lightweight encryption, and edge-native processing, validated on a Raspberry Pi testbed.
result: Distributed cryptographic processing reduces latency compared to sequential designs while maintaining feasible resource overhead.
conclusion: The framework demonstrates a viable path toward secure, quantum-resilient IoMT systems, with future work on energy-aware architectures and intelligent security optimization.

title: Direct Single-shot Imaging Of Time-resolved Terahertz Vector Fields
authors: J. Lafreniere-Greig, J. E. Nkeck, X. Ropagnol, G. Gandubert, Salim Hmidi, O. Brincoveanu, O. -G. Simionescu, E. Abraham, R. Tudor, F. Blanchard
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate direct single-shot retrieval of the full in-plane vector field of broadband terahertz waves using electro-optic sampling. Implemented with a circularly polarized optical probe and polarization-sensitive camera, the method overcomes the projection constraints of conventional electro-optic sampling and enables direct time-domain reconstruction of transverse vector fields without Fourier-domain inversion or sequential polarization analysis. We experimentally validate the approach through spatiotemporal imaging of linear, circular, azimuthal and radial terahertz fields generated by polarization-engineered silicon metamaterials. The measurements reveal ultrafast time-resolved vector-field dynamics inaccessible to conventional scalar detection, including helicoidal field rotation within a single optical cycle and the spatiotemporal evolution of structured polarization topologies. Beyond structured-field imaging, we demonstrate single-scan vector-field spectroscopy through measurements of quartz birefringence and broadband terahertz waveplate performance. More broadly, this work transforms electro-optic sampling from a projection-based measurement into a vector-resolved imaging and spectroscopy platform for structured electromagnetic fields.
tldr: This paper presents a method for direct single-shot imaging of time-resolved terahertz vector fields using electro-optic sampling with a circularly polarized probe and polarization-sensitive camera.
motivation: Conventional electro-optic sampling is projection-based and cannot capture full vector fields in a single shot, limiting the study of structured terahertz fields.
method: The authors use a circularly polarized optical probe and a polarization-sensitive camera to simultaneously measure both orthogonal components of the terahertz field, enabling direct time-domain reconstruction without Fourier inversion.
result: They experimentally validate the technique by imaging linear, circular, azimuthal, and radial terahertz fields from polarization-engineered silicon metamaterials, revealing ultrafast vector-field dynamics and demonstrating single-scan vector-field spectroscopy.
conclusion: This work transforms electro-optic sampling into a vector-resolved imaging and spectroscopy platform for structured electromagnetic fields.

title: Analysis Of A Compact Interferometric Imager
authors: Laurent M. Mugnier, Vincent Michau, Hiyam Debary, Fr\'ed\'eric Cassaing
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The advent of photonic integrated circuits (PICs) will allow the replacement of the large aperture of an optical telescope by a dense array of small apertures combined interferometically. The light coming from aperture pairs can be combined by a PIC in order to extract interferogram characteristics known as complex visibilities, from which the observed object can then be reconstructed. In such a compact interferometric imager, the optical components dedicated to image formation in a regular telescope are no longer necessary. In particular, such a concept is relevant for space missions where weight and size are critical. In this communication, we study such an instrument concept, focusing on signal-to-noise considerations. We recall the design basis for the field and the spatial resolution, and we show that the spectral resolution must be no less than the field to resolution ratio. Then, we analyze the signal-to-noise ratio of this concept, assuming that each spatial frequency is recorded only once, and compare the signal-to-noise ratio with that of a monolithic telescope. We perform the comparison in Fourier space for an identical number of recorded photons. We show that the noise propagation of the interferometric imager is identical to that of a monolithic telescope that would have a flat Modulation Transfer Function with a level roughly given by the ratio of the small apertures' diameter to the maximum baseline. We conclude that the noise propagation in low and medium spatial frequencies is unfavorable for the interferometric imager.
tldr: This paper analyzes the signal-to-noise ratio of a compact interferometric imager using photonic integrated circuits, comparing it to a monolithic telescope.
motivation: To replace large telescope apertures with dense arrays of small apertures combined interferometrically for space missions where weight and size are critical.
method: The authors derive design basis for field and spatial resolution, show spectral resolution constraints, and compare noise propagation in Fourier space assuming identical photon counts.
result: Noise propagation of the interferometric imager is identical to a monolithic telescope with a flat Modulation Transfer Function at a level given by the ratio of small aperture diameter to maximum baseline.
conclusion: The interferometric imager has unfavorable noise propagation at low and medium spatial frequencies compared to a monolithic telescope.

title: Nodal Degeneration Of Chiral Algebras Ii: Local Structure And Chiral Zhu Algebras
authors: Elchanan Nafcha
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a vertex algebra [MATH], Zhu constructed an associative algebra [MATH], whose representation theory provides an approximation to the category of [MATH]-modules. We describe a geometric construction of a certain derived associative algebra [MATH] associated to any universal factorization algebra [MATH], whose zeroth homology recovers Zhu's associative algebra in the case where [MATH] is obtained from a vertex algebra. The construction is given by integrating [MATH] over stable configurations parametrized by two-pointed semistable genus zero curves. By a variant of this construction, we obtained a chiral [MATH]-bimodule [MATH] describing the value of a factorization algebra at a nodal point. We show that its zeroth homology recovers the bimodule underlying the mode-transition algebra [MATH] defined by Damiolini, Gibney, and Krashen, which they use to describes a vertex algebra at a node. Finally, the value over a formal smoothing of a node provides a deformation [MATH] of [MATH], whose zeroth homology describes a deformation of the mode-transition algebra in the case of a vertex algebra.
tldr: This paper develops a geometric construction of a derived associative algebra from a universal factorization algebra, recovering Zhu's algebra and mode-transition algebras for vertex algebras.
motivation: To provide a geometric framework for understanding the representation theory of vertex algebras, particularly at nodal points on curves.
method: The construction integrates a factorization algebra over stable configurations parametrized by two-pointed semistable genus zero curves, and studies deformations via formal smoothings of nodes.
result: The zeroth homology of the constructed algebra recovers Zhu's associative algebra and the bimodule underlying the mode-transition algebra of Damiolini, Gibney, and Krashen.
conclusion: The geometric approach yields a deformation of the mode-transition algebra, offering new insights into vertex algebra structures at nodes.

title: Proof And More Variations Of Bellman's Lost-in-a-forest Problem
authors: Zhipeng Deng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, based on our previous general formulation and computational solution to Bellman's Lost-in-a-forest Problem, we provide the proof of general solution and obtained more variations and results related to this problem. This paper provides generalized formalized method connecting curve covering, lost-in-the-forest problem, and traveling salesman problem with neighborhoods. We prove the equivalence and convergence. We also provide more results of searching for two lines, connection to Wetzel's unit arc covering problem, variations with closed path, variations in three dimensions, etc. The results include general calculation equations, partial analytical results, and numerical results.
tldr: This paper provides proofs and variations of Bellman's lost-in-a-forest problem, a geometric optimization problem about curve covering and search paths.
motivation: To generalize and prove the solution to Bellman's lost-in-a-forest problem and explore its connections to other covering problems.
method: The authors use formalized methods connecting curve covering, lost-in-the-forest problem, and traveling salesman problem with neighborhoods, proving equivalence and convergence.
result: They provide general calculation equations, partial analytical results, and numerical results for various settings including two lines, Wetzel's problem, closed paths, and three dimensions.
conclusion: The work extends the theoretical understanding of search and covering problems but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Theory And Applications Of Convolution-Based Short Time Offset Linear Canonical Transform
authors: Gita Rani Mahato, Manab Kundu, Alit Elsa Xavier
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a convolution based short time offset linear canonical transform (STOLCT) and investigate its fundamental mathematical properties. Specifically, we establish its continuity, orthogonality relations, inversion formulas, range theorem, and convolution theorem. We further explore several important applications of STOLCT, including the Poisson summation formula, the Paley Wiener criterion, and a sampling theorem. In addition, numerical simulations and graphical analyses are presented to compare signal reconstruction performance under different scenarios. A comparative study between STOLCT and STLCT is conducted with respect to their reconstruction formulas, demonstrating the effectiveness and potential advantages of the proposed transform.
tldr: This paper introduces a convolution-based short time offset linear canonical transform and studies its mathematical properties and signal processing applications.
motivation: To generalize the short time linear canonical transform by incorporating a convolution operation, enabling better signal reconstruction and analysis.
method: The authors define the STOLCT, prove its continuity, orthogonality, inversion, range, and convolution theorems, and derive Poisson summation, Paley-Wiener, and sampling theorems. Numerical simulations compare reconstruction performance.
result: The STOLCT is shown to be a valid transform with desirable mathematical properties, and numerical experiments demonstrate its effectiveness over the standard STLCT in certain scenarios.
conclusion: The proposed transform offers potential advantages for signal processing, but the paper is purely mathematical and unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Zhu's Algebra And The $C_2$-algebra Of A Classically Free Vertex Operator Algebra
authors: Xianlong Zeng Bailin Song
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, for a classically free vertex algebra, the [MATH]-algebra is naturally isomorphic to the associated graded algebra of Zhu's algebra. As an application, we show that non-trivial holomorphic VOAs of CFT type are not classically free. This includes the affine vertex operator algebra of [MATH] at level one, as well as the Moonshine VOA.
tldr: This paper proves an isomorphism between Zhu's algebra and the C2-algebra for classically free vertex algebras, and applies it to show that non-trivial holomorphic VOAs of CFT type are not classically free.
motivation: To understand the structure of vertex operator algebras (VOAs) and their associated graded algebras, particularly for classically free VOAs.
method: Algebraic and categorical methods in vertex algebra theory, constructing isomorphisms between Zhu's algebra and the C2-algebra.
result: The C2-algebra of a classically free vertex algebra is naturally isomorphic to the associated graded algebra of Zhu's algebra. Non-trivial holomorphic VOAs of CFT type, including the affine VOA of E8 at level one and the Moonshine VOA, are not classically free.
conclusion: Classical freeness is a restrictive condition that excludes many important VOAs, providing insight into the structure of holomorphic VOAs.

title: From Phase Semantics To Base-extension Semantics (and Back)
authors: Ekaterina Piotrovskaya
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linear logic admits a wide range of semantic presentations reflecting its resource-sensitive notion of consequence. One well-known example is phase semantics: an algebraic semantics in which formulas are interpreted in phase spaces, consisting of a commutative monoid and a fixed subset, with respect to which an orthogonality relation is defined. A rather different and much more recent approach is given by base-extension semantics, which defines validity by inductively extending a provability relation on a base -- a set of inference rules over atomic propositions. We establish an equivalence between the two semantics by first defining bidirectional maps between bases and phase spaces, and then constructing an isomorphism between a phase space (resp. base) and its image under the composition of these maps. As a further contribution, we define the base-extension semantics clauses for the exponentials of linear logic.
tldr: The paper establishes an equivalence between phase semantics and base-extension semantics for linear logic, including clauses for exponentials.
motivation: To bridge two distinct semantic approaches for linear logic, which have different conceptual foundations and applications.
method: Defines bidirectional maps between bases and phase spaces, then constructs an isomorphism between a phase space (or base) and its image under composition of these maps.
result: An equivalence between phase semantics and base-extension semantics is proven, and base-extension semantics is extended to handle the exponentials of linear logic.
conclusion: The two semantics are essentially equivalent, providing a unified perspective on the resource-sensitive semantics of linear logic.

title: Crypto X Ai, Ai X Crypto: A Survey
authors: Sarah Allen, Pranay Anchuri, James Austgen, Maryam Bahrani, Samuel Breckenridge, Aaron Buchwald, Christian Cachin, Andr\'es F\'abrega, Jared Fernandez, James Hsin-Yu Chiang, Marwa Mouallem, Roi Bar-Zur, Neil Desilva, Ittay Eyal, Giulia Fanti, Ari Juels, Andrew Miller, Christian Sillaber, Dani Vilardell, Pramod Viswanath, Wenhao Wang, Matt Weinberg, Sen Yang, Jianzhu Yao, Fan Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13892v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The intersection of crypto x AI is spawning papers, products, online posts, and companies. All the surrounding buzz, though, obscures what exactly has been done, what the opportunities and challenges are, and what open questions deserve attention. This survey paper asks what AI can do for blockchain-based technologies (broadly construed as "crypto") (crypto x AI), and vice versa (AI x crypto). We systematize existing work, summarize key takeaways, highlight open research questions, and offer a perspective on pervasive industry misconceptions, concluding that AI and crypto are still in the very early stages of meaningful integration.
tldr: A survey of the intersection between AI and blockchain technologies, covering applications and open questions.
motivation: To systematize the growing body of work at the intersection of AI and crypto, clarify opportunities and challenges, and correct industry misconceptions.
method: The authors review existing literature and industry developments, categorize approaches, and summarize key takeaways.
result: The survey finds that AI and crypto are still in early stages of meaningful integration, with many open research questions.
conclusion: AI and crypto have potential synergies but require further research and development for practical integration.

title: An Entropy Potential For Type-Composition Games
authors: Morteza Alimi, Merlin de la Haye, Pascal Lenzner, \v{s}imon Schierreich, Alexander Skopalik, Marcus Wunderlich
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Potential functions are a key tool in theoretical computer science with applications ranging from the runtime analysis of algorithms and data structures, through the analysis of the expected behavior of random processes and search heuristics, to proving the existence of equilibrium states in strategic games. Typically, proofs that employ potential functions are short, elegant, and easy to verify, yet very powerful. Moreover, potential functions are essential ingredients for constructive proofs, in particular in algorithmic game theory. There, a key question is the existence of equilibrium states, but the most powerful theorem in the field -- Nash's theorem -- is unfortunately non-constructive. For many strategic games, potential functions come to the rescue by enabling constructive proofs that sometimes even yield efficient algorithms for finding equilibria. We add to this by providing a novel class of entropy-inspired log-multinomial potential functions for natural game-theoretic settings where rational agents of different types strategically choose actions to maximize their utility. In particular, we consider utility functions that are based on the fraction of same- and other-type agents taking the same action. We demonstrate the versatility of the new potential function class by presenting simple equilibrium existence proofs for two recent game-theoretic models, for which only involved technical proofs were previously known. Even better, the new potential function class yields efficient algorithms for constructing equilibria for much more general models. Thereby, we positively resolve several open problems.
tldr: This paper introduces entropy-inspired potential functions for type-composition games in algorithmic game theory, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To provide constructive proofs of equilibrium existence in strategic games where agents' utilities depend on the fraction of same- and other-type agents taking the same action.
method: The authors define a novel class of log-multinomial potential functions based on entropy, and apply them to two recent game-theoretic models.
result: The new potential functions yield simple equilibrium existence proofs and efficient algorithms for constructing equilibria, resolving several open problems.
conclusion: The entropy-inspired potential functions are a versatile tool for equilibrium analysis in type-composition games.

title: History Of The Muddy Children Puzzle
authors: Hans van Ditmarsch
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13703v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Muddy Children Puzzle is a puzzle about knowledge and ignorance that has been inspiring for the development of epistemic logic. Who came up with it first? This is unclear. We trace the origin of the Muddy Children Puzzle through logical and literary publications over the past two centuries. The puzzle inspired a numerous variations such as involving numbers or coloured hats. We also present a novel hats puzzle involving self-reference.
tldr: A historical and literary tracing of the origin and variations of the Muddy Children Puzzle, a classic epistemic logic problem.
motivation: To clarify the unclear origin of the Muddy Children Puzzle and document its evolution through logical and literary publications over two centuries.
method: Historical literature review and logical analysis of puzzle variations, including a novel self-referential hats puzzle.
result: Traces the puzzle's roots to 19th-century publications and presents a new variation involving self-reference.
conclusion: The puzzle's origin remains ambiguous, but its influence on epistemic logic is well-documented; the new variation adds to the family of knowledge puzzles.

title: Ai Can Help Scientists Publish Less
authors: Gianfranco Bertone
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We can do more than defend science from a flood of AI-assisted papers. Used well, AI offers a historic opportunity to correct distortions in the publication system, help us publish fewer and better papers, and give scientists back the time to do their best work.
tldr: This paper discusses how AI can help reduce the number of scientific publications and improve their quality, focusing on the publication system rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The author argues that the current scientific publication system is flooded with low-quality papers, partly due to AI-assisted writing, and proposes using AI to correct these distortions.
method: The paper is an opinion piece or commentary, not presenting a specific technical method.
result: No empirical results; the paper advocates for a cultural shift in publishing practices.
conclusion: AI offers an opportunity to publish fewer but better papers, giving scientists more time for meaningful research.

title: A Betchov-Type Hydrodynamic Formulation Of The Ivancevic Option-Pricing Equation
authors: Sandeep Kumar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13881v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that, under constant-coefficient assumptions, the Ivancevic option-pricing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation admits a Betchov-type hydrodynamic formulation analogous to the one appearing in the context of the vortex filament equation. We identify the corresponding continuity equation and momentum-type conservation law satisfied by the density--velocity pair and illustrate the formulation on known Ivancevic-type soliton solutions. The resulting interpretation is structural and model-dependent, and is intended as a bridge between nonlinear wave formulations in mathematical finance and geometric fluid mechanics.
tldr: This paper derives a hydrodynamic formulation of the Ivancevic option-pricing equation, linking nonlinear wave models in finance to geometric fluid mechanics.
motivation: To bridge nonlinear wave formulations in mathematical finance with geometric fluid mechanics via a Betchov-type hydrodynamic analogy.
method: Assuming constant coefficients, the Ivancevic nonlinear Schrödinger equation is recast into a continuity equation and momentum-type conservation law, analogous to the vortex filament equation.
result: A Betchov-type hydrodynamic formulation is obtained, and the density-velocity pair is illustrated on known soliton solutions.
conclusion: The interpretation is structural and model-dependent, serving as a conceptual bridge between finance and fluid dynamics.

title: Hybrid Dynamics Of Rocking Blocks Beyond Overturning: Saltation Analysis, Bifurcations, And Stability Characterization
authors: Fernando Gaibor E., Alexander L\'opez, Esther D. Guti\'errez
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work investigates how restitution modeling affects the dynamics of rocking blocks subjected to harmonic excitation. While several studies have reported discrepancies between experimentally observed impact behavior and the predictions obtained using the classical Housner restitution coefficient, the implications of adopting alternative restitution formulations on the global dynamics of rocking systems remain largely unexplored. The system is formulated as a hybrid non-smooth dynamical model and analyzed through bifurcation diagrams, Lyapunov exponents, and basins of attraction for different slenderness ratios. By comparing the classical restitution model proposed by Housner with the alternative formulation of Mao et al., we show that the choice of restitution model strongly influences the predicted system response. The alternative formulation leads to an earlier onset and greater prevalence of complex oscillations, as well as changes in the type, stability, and accessibility of attractors compared to the classical model. However, as the slenderness ratio increases, the dynamical features produced by both formulations progressively converge, indicating a reduced sensitivity to the restitution model for taller blocks. These results provide a dynamical perspective on why alternative restitution formulations, which predict impact responses closer to experimental observations, can produce markedly different behaviors from those obtained using the classical Housner model.
tldr: This paper studies the nonlinear dynamics of rocking blocks under harmonic excitation, focusing on the influence of restitution models on bifurcations and stability.
motivation: Experimental observations of rocking block impacts deviate from classical Housner model predictions, motivating exploration of alternative restitution formulations.
method: The system is modeled as a hybrid non-smooth dynamical system and analyzed via bifurcation diagrams, Lyapunov exponents, and basins of attraction for varying slenderness ratios.
result: The alternative restitution model (Mao et al.) yields earlier onset and greater prevalence of complex oscillations, with differences diminishing for taller blocks.
conclusion: Restitution model choice significantly affects predicted dynamics, explaining discrepancies between experiments and classical theory.

title: Compact Photonic Fibre-based Deformation Sensor Fabricated By Two-Photon Polymerization
authors: Vladimir Osipov, Ayman El-Tamer, Ulf Hinze, Alexander Dulebo, David J. Webb
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We have demonstrated that compact deformation sensors with heights and widths of about 100 micrometers can be fabricated by two-photon polymerization, using commercially available optical ferrules with embedded 125 micrometers-diameter optical fibers as the basic platform and the commercial photopolymers OrmoComp and FemtoBond as the fabrication materials.
tldr: A compact deformation sensor fabricated by two-photon polymerization on optical fibers.
motivation: To create small, robust deformation sensors for structural health monitoring.
method: Two-photon polymerization is used to fabricate polymer structures on optical fiber ferrules.
result: Sensors with ~100 μm dimensions are demonstrated using commercial materials.
conclusion: The approach enables compact, integrable deformation sensors.

title: Wealth Inequality And Planetary Boundaries In A Stylized Agent-Based Model
authors: Thomas Valade, Michael Benzaquen, Matthieu Cristelli, Stanislao Gualdi, Pierre Lenders
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: At the intersection of rising wealth inequality and intensifying environmental pressures, we investigate a reverse causal relationship that has received comparatively little attention: wealth inequality may not only be a consequence of environmental crises, but also act as a structural obstacle to the ecological transition itself. We develop a stylized agent-based model in which heterogeneous agents, whose initial wealth follows a Pareto distribution, allocate their income between either a Brown or a Green sector through a utility function. The function is designed to capture the trade-off between short-term returns and exposure to long-term systemic risks. A central ingredient is that wealthier agents perceive themselves as less vulnerable to environmental shocks, thereby reducing the amount of resources available for the transition. We show that, beyond inequality thresholds compatible with those observed in most developed countries, the economy remains locked in a Brown regime, even when a substantial share of agents is sensitive to externalities. We then assess a set of stylized fiscal policies (basic income, carbon taxation, Green incentives, and a combined scheme) and find that their effectiveness depends strongly on the inequality regime and on the regressivity embedded in the fiscal mechanism, revealing multidimensional trade-offs between transition speed, cumulative environmental destruction, growth, and fiscal pressure.
tldr: This paper uses an agent-based model to study how wealth inequality hinders the ecological transition, focusing on economic and environmental dynamics.
motivation: To explore the reverse causal relationship where wealth inequality acts as a structural obstacle to ecological transition, beyond being a consequence of environmental crises.
method: A stylized agent-based model with heterogeneous agents allocating income between Brown and Green sectors via a utility function that captures short-term returns vs. long-term systemic risks, with wealthier agents perceiving lower vulnerability.
result: Beyond inequality thresholds observed in developed countries, the economy remains locked in a Brown regime; fiscal policy effectiveness depends on inequality regime and regressivity.
conclusion: Wealth inequality can impede ecological transition, and policies must account for inequality regimes to be effective.

title: Detecting Historical Turning Points In Italian Media: A Complex Systems Approach To A Diachronic News Corpus
authors: Dario Zarcone, Salvatore Miccich\`e, David Sanchez
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing availability of large-scale textual corpora has opened new possibilities for data-driven, quantitative approaches to historical analysis using Natural Language Processing (NLP). However, diachronic corpora with historical relevance from the pre-digital era remain scarce and often incomplete. We present a quantitative approach to historical analysis based on the reconstruction and exploration of a diachronic corpus of around 600,000 articles from the Italian newspaper "La Repubblica", covering all the articles published from the 1st of January 1985 to the 31st of December 2000 - a period of major political, social, and geopolitical change in Italy and globally. Using NLP techniques, we analyze the text at both lexical and semantic levels; we then apply tools from complex systems and statistical physics to trace shifts in media discourse over time. This allows us to detect key transition periods, such as the transition from the First Republic to the Second Republic in Italy, or major international conflicts like the Gulf War or the Kosovo War, without relying on prior labeling. The results show how combining computational linguistics with ideas from complex systems can offer new quantitative insight into historical changes, opening up new paths for studying the dynamics of media and society through large-scale textual data.
tldr: This paper applies NLP and complex systems methods to a diachronic news corpus to detect historical turning points in Italian media.
motivation: To provide a quantitative, data-driven approach to historical analysis using large-scale textual data from pre-digital era newspapers.
method: Reconstructs a corpus of 600,000 articles from La Repubblica (1985-2000), applies NLP for lexical and semantic analysis, and uses complex systems/statistical physics tools to trace shifts in media discourse.
result: Detects key transition periods such as the shift from First to Second Republic in Italy and major international conflicts without prior labeling.
conclusion: Combining computational linguistics with complex systems offers new quantitative insights into historical changes and media dynamics.

title: On The Convergence Of The Normalized Power Sequence Of Riesz Operators
authors: Renu Shekhawat Soumyashant Nayak
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a complex Hilbert space and [MATH] be the algebra of all bounded linear operators on [MATH]. For [MATH], let [MATH]. We refer to the sequence [MATH] as the NPS (normalized power sequence) of [MATH]. In this article, we show that the NPS of a Riesz operator [MATH] converges in norm to a positive operator [MATH], and provide an explicit description of the spectral resolution of [MATH] in terms of the Riesz idempotents associated with the non-zero eigenvalues of [MATH]. Since every compact operator is a Riesz operator, this gives us a stronger, spatial generalization of the Yamamoto-Davis theorem, which asserts that [MATH] is equal to the [MATH]-largest eigenvalue-modulus of the compact operator [MATH], where [MATH] denotes the [MATH]-largest singular value. In recent work, the present authors have established the norm convergence of the NPS for spectral operators.
