motivation: To generalize the Yamamoto-Davis theorem for compact operators to Riesz operators and to understand convergence properties of normalized power sequences.
method: The authors use spectral theory of Riesz operators, Riesz idempotents, and a rank-one perturbation of a unitary operator to demonstrate failure of convergence for essentially spectral operators.
result: The normalized power sequence of a Riesz operator converges in norm to a positive operator with explicit spectral resolution; a counterexample shows this fails for essentially spectral operators.
conclusion: The work provides a spatial generalization of the Yamamoto-Davis theorem and clarifies limitations of convergence for broader classes of operators.

title: A WKB-related Time-stepping Scheme For Differential Equations Describing Oscillatory Systems
authors: Rupert Klein Juliane Rosemeier
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, we present a novel time-stepping scheme for multiscale differential equations describing oscillatory systems with well-separated scales, where the scale separation is controlled by a small parameter [MATH]. The time-stepping method is related to a multi-modal WKB approximation and relies on a transformation of variables derived in this work. The analysis reveals that, in the transformed formulation, the leading-order oscillations are either eliminated or appear only at higher asymptotic order. The method is applied to ordinary differential equations, including the well-known van der Pol oscillator. We investigate the accuracy of the proposed method numerically for different parameter regimes, in particular for decreasing values of [MATH], and study how the parameters of the numerical scheme must be adapted as [MATH] is reduced. In the presented numerical tests, the computational cost remains bounded as [MATH] is decreased.
tldr: A numerical time-stepping scheme for multiscale oscillatory ODEs based on WKB approximation.
motivation: To efficiently solve differential equations with well-separated scales where standard methods become costly.
method: Transforms variables using a multi-modal WKB approximation to eliminate leading-order oscillations, then applies a tailored time-stepping scheme.
result: The method maintains bounded computational cost as the small parameter decreases, with accuracy validated on the van der Pol oscillator.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is effective for oscillatory systems with scale separation, offering a practical alternative to conventional solvers.

title: Validated Numerics For The Gauss Problem On Continued Fractions
authors: M. Pollicott
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We get estimates on the Gauss-Kuzmin-Wirsing constant for continued fractions.
tldr: The paper presents validated numerical estimates for the Gauss-Kuzmin-Wirsing constant in continued fractions.
motivation: The Gauss problem on continued fractions is a classical topic in number theory and dynamical systems, and obtaining rigorous bounds on the associated constant is of theoretical interest.
method: The author uses validated numerics (interval arithmetic) to compute rigorous enclosures for the Gauss-Kuzmin-Wirsing constant.
result: The paper provides explicit numerical estimates with guaranteed error bounds for the constant.
conclusion: The work contributes to the rigorous computational study of continued fraction expansions, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Analytic First Derivatives Of Sider Interpolation
authors: Shingyu Leung
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spherical interpolation is required in numerical and geometric applications in which the unknowns are constrained to remain on the unit sphere. Spherical Interpolation of orDER [MATH] (SIDER-[MATH]) was introduced as the high-order reconstruction component of spherical essentially non-oscillatory interpolation, where the reconstruction is built entirely from spherical linear interpolation (SLERP) operations and therefore preserves the spherical constraint exactly. This paper develops analytic first-derivative formulas for SIDER curves of arbitrary order. The central observation is that the recursive definition of SIDER can be differentiated by direct chain-rule propagation through its binary tree of SLERP operations. After deriving the total derivative of SLERP with moving endpoints, we obtain compact recursions for the derivative of SIDER-[MATH], including simplified formulas at interpolation nodes and practical formulas at middle points between consecutive sampling locations. The latter are relevant when a reconstruction is evaluated halfway between data samples, as occurs in several high-order reconstruction-based numerical algorithms. The base case SIDER2 is treated explicitly, and SIDER3 and SIDER4 are used to illustrate the recursive mechanism. We also prove that the derivative is tangent to the sphere at every reconstructed point, including both sampling points and middle points. The resulting formulas extend the original SIDER/SENO framework by supplying differential information for sphere-valued reconstructions, with potential use in high-order finite-volume, ENO/WENO, SENO-type, and related methods for conservation laws and evolution problems.
tldr: This paper derives analytic first-derivative formulas for spherical interpolation of arbitrary order (SIDER) using chain-rule propagation through SLERP operations.
motivation: High-order numerical methods for sphere-valued data require derivative information, which was previously unavailable for SIDER interpolation.
method: The authors differentiate the recursive definition of SIDER by propagating derivatives through the binary tree of SLERP operations, obtaining compact recursions and explicit formulas for low orders.
result: Compact derivative formulas are derived for arbitrary-order SIDER, with explicit treatment for SIDER2, SIDER3, and SIDER4, and it is proved that the derivative is tangent to the sphere at all points.
conclusion: The formulas extend the SIDER/SENO framework to provide differential information, enabling high-order finite-volume and ENO/WENO methods for sphere-valued conservation laws.

title: Pre-vertex Algebras, pre-Poisson Vertex Algebras And Their Deformation Quantizations
authors: Jiefeng Liu Jiabao Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13999v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce pre-vertex algebras and pre-Poisson vertex algebras as preLie-algebras in the chiral and classical pseudo-tensor categories, respectively. We show that a pre-vertex algebra gives rise to a vertex algebra, that every Rota-Baxter operator on a vertex algebra induces a pre-vertex algebra, and that every pre-vertex algebra can be embedded into a vertex algebra equipped with a Rota-Baxter operator. Moreover, we prove that pre-vertex algebras are equivalent to dendriform vertex algebras. In the Poisson setting, we demonstrate that pre-Poisson vertex algebras are obtained from Rota-Baxter operators on Poisson vertex algebras, from filtrations of pre-vertex algebras, and as classical limits of pre-vertex formal deformations of differential Zinbiel algebras. This extends the classical relationships among Rota-Baxter operators, pre-Lie algebras, and Poisson algebras to the framework of vertex algebras.
tldr: This paper introduces pre-vertex algebras and pre-Poisson vertex algebras, extending algebraic structures from pre-Lie algebras to vertex algebras.
motivation: To generalize the classical relationships among Rota-Baxter operators, pre-Lie algebras, and Poisson algebras to the framework of vertex algebras.
method: The authors define pre-vertex algebras and pre-Poisson vertex algebras as pre-Lie algebras in chiral and classical pseudo-tensor categories, and prove equivalences with dendriform vertex algebras.
result: They show that pre-vertex algebras give rise to vertex algebras, are induced by Rota-Baxter operators, and can be embedded into vertex algebras with Rota-Baxter operators. Pre-Poisson vertex algebras are obtained from Rota-Baxter operators, filtrations, and classical limits.
conclusion: The work establishes a new algebraic framework that extends known structures to vertex algebras, but it is purely mathematical with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Semismooth Newton-Based Proximal Augmented Lagrangian Method For Joint Estimation Of Multiple Gaussian Graphical Models With Clustered Structure
authors: Han Wang, Yue Liu, Yong-Jin Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider a class of convex composite optimization problems arising from the joint estimation of clustered multiple Gaussian graphical models. The resulting model combines a log-determinant loss term with a nonsmooth sparse clustered regularizer, which encourages both similar sparsity patterns and consistent edge values across different graphs. We first establish a necessary and sufficient condition under which the solution is block diagonal, enabling a large-scale problem to be decomposed into smaller independent subproblems and substantially reducing computational complexity. To efficiently solve this problem, we develop a proximal augmented Lagrangian method in which each subproblem is handled by a superlinearly convergent semismooth Newton method. Unlike widely used first order methods, our approach fully exploits the underlying second order information through the semismooth Newton framework, thereby achieving faster convergence and improved robustness. The efficiency and robustness of the proposed algorithm are demonstrated through comparisons with state-of-the-art methods on both synthetic and real data sets.
tldr: This paper proposes a semismooth Newton-based proximal augmented Lagrangian method for joint estimation of multiple Gaussian graphical models with clustered structure.
motivation: Joint estimation of multiple Gaussian graphical models is important for understanding network structures across different conditions, but existing methods often suffer from high computational cost and lack of second-order information.
method: The authors formulate the problem as a convex composite optimization with a log-determinant loss and a nonsmooth sparse clustered regularizer. They establish a block diagonal condition for decomposition and develop a proximal augmented Lagrangian method solved by a semismooth Newton method.
result: The proposed algorithm achieves faster convergence and improved robustness compared to state-of-the-art first-order methods on synthetic and real data.
conclusion: The semismooth Newton-based approach effectively exploits second-order information, making it suitable for large-scale joint graphical model estimation.

title: Battery Bidding Under Price Uncertainty In Wholesale Electricity Markets
authors: Madeleine Udell Vincent Yinjun-Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Grid-scale batteries increasingly influence outcomes in wholesale electricity markets, but their observed bid patterns remain difficult to interpret. In particular, bids that appear to reflect strategic withholding may instead arise from rational operations under price uncertainty and risk management. We develop an asset-level model of a price-taking battery that submits stepwise buy and sell bid curves in the day-ahead market under a finite set of price scenarios. The battery chooses quantity--price pairs to maximize a mean--CVaR objective subject to physical and market constraints. A direct formulation is a mixed-integer linear program, but we show that its integer decisions can be removed, yielding an exact linear programming reformulation suitable for empirical analysis. Our empirical results deliver three insights. First, withholding behavior can arise even without market power, because scarce stored energy and uncertain future prices increase the value of holding energy. Second, the effect of uncertainty depends on the state of charge: when stored energy is scarce, greater uncertainty raises sell bid prices, whereas when stored energy is abundant it can lower them. Third, risk management reshapes bid curves into layered structures that secure profitable execution across a broad set of scenarios while preserving some exposure to rare but valuable price spikes.
tldr: This paper models battery bidding in wholesale electricity markets under price uncertainty using a mean-CVaR objective, showing that withholding behavior can arise without market power.
motivation: Grid-scale batteries are increasingly important in electricity markets, but their bidding patterns are hard to interpret; apparent strategic withholding may actually be rational risk management.
method: The authors develop an asset-level model of a price-taking battery that submits stepwise bid curves in the day-ahead market under price scenarios, maximizing a mean-CVaR objective. They reformulate the mixed-integer linear program into an exact linear program.
result: Withholding can occur without market power due to scarce stored energy and price uncertainty; the effect of uncertainty depends on state of charge; risk management produces layered bid structures.
conclusion: Observed bidding patterns in electricity markets can be explained by rational risk-averse operation, not necessarily market power abuse.

title: Confidence Bands For The Gradient Lines Of A Density Function
authors: Wanli Qiao Ery Arias-Castro
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of estimating the gradient ascent line of a density originating at a given point. Going beyond mere consistency, we establish a weak convergence result for a plugin estimator based on a kernel density estimator of the density. We then leverage that result to construct a confidence region for the gradient ascent line, including by bootstrap.
tldr: This paper constructs confidence bands for gradient lines of a density function using kernel density estimation.
motivation: Estimating gradient ascent lines of a density is useful for understanding topological features, but the paper focuses on statistical inference rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: A plug-in estimator based on kernel density estimation is used, and weak convergence is established to construct confidence regions via bootstrap.
result: Weak convergence results for the gradient line estimator are proven, enabling confidence band construction.
conclusion: The work provides a statistical tool for density gradient lines but has no connection to the user's research interests.

title: Robin-Neumann Coupling Of Pinn And Fem Solvers: A Steklov-Poincar\'e View, With Application To Fluid-Structure Interaction With Contact
authors: Mikel Landajuela
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are meshless and carry moving geometry and topology change through resampling of collocation points; the finite-element method (FEM) is the workhorse for boundary-fitted discretisations. Coupling the two across a shared interface promises the best of both, yet existing PINN-FEM schemes are validated only empirically. We put the coupling on a domain-decomposition footing: viewing each solver as a Steklov-Poincar\'e (trace-to-flux) operator, we transfer the classical Dirichlet-Neumann (DN) divergence diagnosis and its Robin-Neumann (RN) cure, including a closed-form, sweep-free interface impedance, and prove a PINN-specific contraction theorem: a trained network realises only a perturbed Steklov operator with a per-step training residual, and RN still contracts, with no shared-eigenbasis hypothesis, to a floor set by the achieved training loss. Because a PINN has no stiffness matrix, we introduce a Fourier-mode interface probe that recovers the network's resolvable Steklov eigenvalues to within 0.5% and doubles as a diagnostic of the network's spectral cap. The theory predicts measured PINN-FEM contraction rates to within 7% on 1D and 2D Poisson couplings, and a two-slab analogue of the large-added-mass regime shows RN's per-mode impedance matching winning decisively where tuned scalar relaxation saturates. We demonstrate the framework on a Stokes/rigid-disc problem with Alart-Curnier contact: the meshless PINN fluid absorbs the topology change at contact by collocation exclusion alone, no remeshing and no cut cells, and the static-equilibrium contact reaction matches the submerged weight to 0.4% under mesh refinement. We quantify remaining limitations: the warm-started PINN drifts off the Stokes manifold over long horizons, and matched FEM-FEM benchmarks attribute pre-impact squeeze-film signatures to PINN under-resolution.
tldr: This paper proposes a theoretical framework for coupling physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) with finite element methods (FEM) using domain decomposition and Steklov-Poincaré operators, with application to fluid-structure interaction with contact.
motivation: Existing PINN-FEM coupling schemes lack rigorous theoretical justification; the authors aim to provide a solid mathematical foundation and prove convergence guarantees.
method: The coupling is formulated as a domain decomposition problem where each solver is treated as a Steklov-Poincaré operator. A Robin-Neumann (RN) coupling is introduced with a closed-form interface impedance, and a contraction theorem is proven accounting for PINN training residuals.
result: The RN coupling contracts to a floor set by the training loss, and a Fourier-mode probe recovers the network's resolvable Steklov eigenvalues to within 0.5%. Measured contraction rates match theory within 7% on Poisson problems, and the method is demonstrated on a Stokes/rigid-disc contact problem.
conclusion: The framework enables meshless handling of topology changes via PINNs without remeshing, but limitations include drift of warm-started PINNs over long horizons and under-resolution of squeeze-film signatures.

title: A Generalized Hacker Dynamics Model With Nonlinear Incidence: Analysis And Positivity-Preserving Numerical Simulation
authors: Manh Tuan Hoang, Hoai Thu Pham, Matthias Ehrhardt
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose and analyze a generalized compartment model for hacker dynamics in cybersecurity systems. This model is an extension of a recently introduced framework, replacing the bilinear interaction term with a broad class of nonlinear incidence functions. This provides greater modeling flexibility and allows for the description of a wider range of cyber-propagation and information-spreading processes. First, we investigate the qualitative dynamics of the model. We establish the positivity and boundedness of solutions, derive the basic reproduction number, and characterize the existence of hacker-free and hacker-present equilibria. We obtain local and global asymptotic stability results, yielding a complete description of the global dynamics in terms of the basic reproduction number. Next, we develop a second-order, positivity-preserving, nonstandard finite difference (NSFD) scheme for numerical simulations. Unlike many existing NSFD approaches, which are typically first-order accurate, the proposed method achieves second-order convergence while preserving positivity for arbitrary step sizes. Furthermore, the proposed method reproduces the asymptotic stability properties of the continuous model, making it suitable for long-time simulations. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical results and demonstrate the superior accuracy and qualitative performance of the proposed scheme compared to several first-order methods.
tldr: This paper proposes and analyzes a generalized compartment model for hacker dynamics in cybersecurity using nonlinear incidence functions and develops a second-order positivity-preserving numerical scheme.
motivation: To extend existing hacker dynamics models with more flexible nonlinear incidence functions and to develop a more accurate numerical method for simulation.
method: Qualitative analysis of the compartment model (positivity, boundedness, equilibria, stability) and construction of a second-order nonstandard finite difference scheme that preserves positivity and stability.
result: Complete characterization of global dynamics via the basic reproduction number and a second-order NSFD scheme that outperforms first-order methods in accuracy and qualitative fidelity.
conclusion: The proposed model and numerical scheme provide a robust framework for simulating hacker dynamics with improved accuracy and reliability.

title: A New Primal-Dual Algorithm With Convex Combination And Extrapolation For Convex-Concave Saddle Point Problems With Nonlinear Coupling Term
authors: Jialong Li, Zexian Liu, Xiaokai Chang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Convex-concave saddle point problems with nonlinear coupling term have wide applications in signal processing, machine learning, robust optimization, and generative models, among others. Primal-dual algorithms are widely used for convex-concave saddle point problems. However, when handling nonlinear coupling term in convex-concave saddle point problems, primal-dual algorithms usually encounter geometric mismatches between variable and mapping spaces, delayed gradient information, and strong dependence on linesearch, resulting in less stable performance and complex convergence analysis. To address these issues, we propose a new primal-dual algorithm named PDAce by combining convex combination and extrapolation strategies. More specifically, in the update of the primal variable, we construct a convex combination point to replace the current iterative point and compute the Jacobian matrix of the vector function in the nonlinear coupling term at the convex combination point. Besides, we use the latest information of convex combination points to extend extrapolation to the mapping space in the update of the dual variable. The core innovations lie in performing linearization of the vector function in the nonlinear coupling term at convex combination points and shifting extrapolation from the variable space to the nonlinear mapping space. This design completely eliminates nonlinear residual terms and allows for rigorous convergence analysis without linesearch. Under mild convex assumptions, we construct a new Lyapunov potential function to prove that PDAce is globally convergent with an ergodic convergence rate of [MATH]. Moreover, we develop an accelerated version of PDAce, termed aPDAce, which achieves [MATH] rate under strong convexity of the primal function, and linear convergence when both the primal and dual functions are strongly convex.
tldr: This paper proposes a new primal-dual algorithm for convex-concave saddle point problems with nonlinear coupling, achieving improved convergence rates without linesearch.
motivation: Existing primal-dual algorithms for nonlinear coupling suffer from geometric mismatches, delayed gradients, and reliance on linesearch, leading to unstable performance and complex analysis.
method: The algorithm PDAce uses a convex combination point for primal update and extrapolation in the mapping space for dual update, eliminating nonlinear residual terms and enabling rigorous convergence analysis without linesearch.
result: PDAce achieves global convergence with ergodic rate O(1/N), and its accelerated version aPDAce achieves O(1/N^2) under strong convexity and linear convergence when both functions are strongly convex.
conclusion: The proposed algorithms provide a stable and efficient solution for saddle point problems with nonlinear coupling, with theoretical guarantees and no need for linesearch.

title: Universal $L^2$-approximation Using Median Digital-net Algorithms
authors: Ziyang Ye, Xiaoqun Wang, Zexin Pan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a median digital-net algorithm for [MATH]-approximation of non-periodic functions over [MATH], inspired by the recently developed median lattice algorithms for the periodic setting. The algorithm requires no smoothness or weight parameters but only a sufficiently large candidate Walsh index set [MATH]. It proceeds in three stages: generating multiple estimates of the Walsh coefficients in [MATH] using independent randomized digital-net samples; taking the respective median of both the estimates and their absolute values; then, based on these median values, identifying the dominant coefficients and constructing a truncated Walsh series as the final approximation. We prove that if the target function has dominating mixed partial derivatives up to order [MATH], all having finite Vitali variation of fractional order [MATH], then the algorithm achieves an [MATH]-error of [MATH] with high probability, where [MATH] is the total number of function evaluations and [MATH] is arbitrarily small. Furthermore, the implied constant grows at most polynomially in the dimension [MATH] under suitable decay conditions on the ANOVA components of the target function. On the implementation side, we provide both parameter-dependent and -independent constructions of the index set [MATH], and employ the fast Walsh--Hadamard transform and Gray code to accelerate the algorithm. motivation: To develop a parameter-free approximation method for non-periodic functions that works in high dimensions without requiring smoothness or weight parameters.
method: The algorithm generates multiple Walsh coefficient estimates via randomized digital nets, takes medians to identify dominant coefficients, and constructs a truncated Walsh series approximation.
result: The algorithm achieves an L2-error of O(N^{-r} (log N)^{(d-1)/2}) with high probability for functions with mixed partial derivatives of order r, with constants polynomial in dimension under suitable ANOVA decay.
conclusion: The median digital-net algorithm is effective for high-dimensional non-periodic function approximation, supported by numerical experiments.

title: Normal Forms For Rough Differential Equations
authors: Gideon Chiusole, Christian Kuehn, Maximilian Semenowicz
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address the existence of normal forms for rough ordinary differential equations. We assume suitable smoothness and the hyperbolicity of an equilibrium point. In this context, we establish local formal equivalence of the two solution flows generated by a random nonlinear RDE and its linearized version. This provides the foundation for extending normal form theory to rough differential equations.
tldr: This paper develops normal form theory for rough differential equations, a topic in stochastic analysis and dynamical systems.
motivation: To extend normal form theory, a classical tool for simplifying dynamical systems near equilibria, to rough differential equations driven by irregular signals.
method: The authors assume smoothness and hyperbolicity of an equilibrium, then establish local formal equivalence between the flow of a nonlinear rough differential equation and its linearization.
result: They prove that under suitable conditions, the nonlinear flow can be formally conjugated to its linear part via a near-identity transformation.
conclusion: This provides a foundation for applying normal form techniques to rough differential equations, enabling further analysis of their qualitative behavior.

title: Primal Finite Element Scheme Of The Hodge-Laplace Problem
authors: Shuo Zhang Wenyu Dong

title: Operator Calculus For Population-Based Optimization: A Mean-Field Convergence Theory
authors: Pekka Malo, Lauri Viitasaari, Patrik Nummi, Antti Suominen, Ankur Sinha, Olli Tahvonen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Population-based and distributional optimization methods, from evolution strategies and consensus-based optimization to covariance-matrix adaptation and stochastic gradient methods viewed as distributional dynamics, are widely used for nonconvex or black-box problems, yet their convergence analyses remain fragmented across algorithm-specific techniques. We introduce an operator calculus in which a broad class of such methods, after choosing an appropriate state space and, where necessary, augmenting the state by memory or strategy variables, is described as a composition of three elementary operators (mutation, selection, and recombination) acting on probability measures. Under explicit stability and regularity conditions, the composite operator admits a pre-generator whose continuous-time limit is a transport-reaction-jump (TRJ) PDE that preserves the operator splitting. On this foundation we establish a modular Lyapunov principle. If a state-space Lyapunov function both dissipates under the full generator and controls the relevant search-space gauges, then the state-space Lyapunov functional and the induced search errors decay exponentially. The additive generator structure allows dissipation estimates to be assembled operator by operator, providing a toolkit for certifying convergence of composite mean-field algorithms.
tldr: This paper develops an operator calculus for population-based optimization algorithms, deriving mean-field convergence via a transport-reaction-jump PDE.
motivation: Convergence analyses of population-based optimization methods are fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors represent algorithms as compositions of mutation, selection, and recombination operators on probability measures, and derive a continuous-time limit PDE with a modular Lyapunov principle.
result: Under stability conditions, exponential convergence of state-space Lyapunov functionals and search errors is established.
conclusion: The operator calculus provides a modular toolkit for certifying convergence of composite mean-field algorithms.

title: Taming Slivers: A Robust Tfem Framework For Reliable Computations On Degenerate Tetrahedral Meshes
authors: Antoine Quiriny, Jonathan Lambrechts, Nicolas Mo\"es, V\'aclav Ku\v{c}era, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Remacle
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sliver elements are an intrinsic difficulty of three-dimensional tetrahedral mesh generation and remain costly, and sometimes impractical, to eliminate completely. Although isolated degenerate elements do not necessarily prevent finite element convergence, connected clusters or sheets of slivers may impose artificial constraints on the discrete solution, leading to locking and severe loss of accuracy. In this work, we revisit the effect of slivers from the viewpoint of the finite element solution and propose a robust solver-side treatment based on the Tempered Finite Element Method (TFEM). The method limits the singular contribution of degenerate elements by introducing a lower bound on the Jacobian determinant, which can be interpreted as a vanishing added-volume correction. The resulting formulation prevents the effective element volume from falling below a threshold while preserving the relevant physical modes of the solution. We analyze the stiffness matrices of degenerate tetrahedra, identify the mechanisms responsible for locking in sliver bands, and assess the method on a range of representative physical problems, including incompressible flow, Cahn--Hilliard phase-field dynamics, transient wave propagation, and vibro-acoustic fluid--structure interaction. The numerical results show that TFEM consistently recovers accurate and physically meaningful solutions on meshes for which standard FEM exhibits locking or loss of convergence, providing a simple and broadly applicable alternative to exhaustive geometric sliver removal.
tldr: This paper proposes a Tempered Finite Element Method to handle sliver tetrahedral elements in mesh generation for computational mechanics.
motivation: Sliver elements in tetrahedral meshes cause locking and loss of accuracy in finite element simulations, and removing them is costly or impractical.
method: The method introduces a lower bound on the Jacobian determinant to limit the singular contribution of degenerate elements, interpreted as a vanishing added-volume correction.
result: TFEM recovers accurate solutions on meshes where standard FEM fails, demonstrated on incompressible flow, phase-field dynamics, wave propagation, and fluid-structure interaction.
conclusion: TFEM provides a simple, broadly applicable alternative to exhaustive geometric sliver removal for reliable computations on degenerate meshes.

title: Stability Of Synthetic Ricci Curvature Lower Bounds For Inverse Limit Extended Metric Measure Spaces
authors: Takumi Yokota Kohei Suzuki
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that every Polish extended metric measure space arises as an inverse limit of metric measure spaces up to isomorphism. We then prove that synthetic Ricci curvature lower bounds and several functional inequalities, including the log-Sobolev, Talagrand, Poincar\'e, and dimension-free Harnack inequalities are stable under inverse limit. We discuss applications to infinite-dimensional spaces, including abstract Wiener spaces and their quotient spaces.
tldr: This paper studies stability of synthetic Ricci curvature lower bounds under inverse limits of metric measure spaces, with applications to infinite-dimensional spaces like abstract Wiener spaces.
motivation: To understand geometric properties of infinite-dimensional spaces that arise as limits of finite-dimensional metric measure spaces.
method: Proves that every Polish extended metric measure space is an inverse limit of metric measure spaces, then shows stability of curvature bounds and functional inequalities under such limits.
result: Synthetic Ricci curvature lower bounds and inequalities (log-Sobolev, Talagrand, Poincaré, Harnack) are stable under inverse limits.
conclusion: Infinite-dimensional spaces like abstract Wiener spaces inherit curvature bounds and functional inequalities from their finite-dimensional approximations.

title: Rates Of Decay For $(\alpha, \beta)$-Ritt-Kreiss Operators
authors: Loris Arnold
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the growth of the sequences [MATH] for bounded linear operators on Banach spaces under various resolvent conditions. Focusing on [MATH]-Ritt operators that are also strongly Kreiss bounded, we show that the growth estimates established by Nevanlinna for Kreiss bounded operators can be significantly refined within the Hilbert space setting, nearly attaining the optimal rates obtained by Seifert for the more restrictive power-bounded case. We further introduce the class of [MATH]-RK operators as a generalization of both Ritt and Kreiss-type conditions. For these operators, we derive comprehensive growth estimates which, for certain ranges of [MATH] and [MATH], yield improvements over existing bounds in the literature. Particular attention is given to [MATH]-Kreiss operators, for which we provide a characterization via Ces\`aro-type means. We show that, in contrast to the well-known case [MATH], the power growth estimate [MATH] is sharp whenever [MATH]. The optimality of our estimates is discussed in several cases, relying on constructions and techniques developed by Nevanlinna, Spijker, and Borovykh. motivation: To refine growth estimates for certain classes of bounded linear operators under resolvent conditions.
method: Uses functional analysis techniques, including resolvent conditions and Cesàro means, to derive and prove sharp growth bounds.
result: Obtains improved growth estimates for (α,β)-Ritt-Kreiss operators and characterizes α-Kreiss operators via Cesàro means.
conclusion: The estimates are sharp in several cases, and a new characterization of Ritt operators is provided.

title: Mathematical Modeling Of Salt Precipitation And Multi-Phase Flow In High Enthalpy Fractured Geothermal Systems
authors: Micheal B. Oguntola, Omar Duran, Eirik Keilegavlen, Inga Berre
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulating high-enthalpy fractured geothermal reservoirs is challenging due to the complex coupled processes of non-isothermal, multiphase, multicomponent flow, strongly nonlinear thermodynamics, and the dominant role of fractures. These complexities are amplified by mineral scaling, such as halite precipitation, which can impair reservoir permeability and well productivity. To address this, we present a new compositional flow model based on a persistent set of primary variables (pressure, enthalpy, and overall salt mass fraction). The formulation naturally handles phase transitions without manual switching, enhancing numerical stability. The model integrates a discrete fracture-matrix approach and employs an efficient, robust correlation-based phase-behaviour linearisation of saltwater thermodynamics, replacing expensive on-the-fly phase separation calculations. It incorporates the Kozeny-Carman relation to dynamically model porosity and permeability reduction from halite precipitation. Implemented in the open-source PorePy framework, the model is verified through a 1D salt dissolution benchmark against the established closed-source simulator CSMP++, showing strong agreement across geothermal conditions involving transitions between single- and multi-phase regions. Application to a 2D halite-saturated fractured reservoir with injection and production demonstrates the model's capability to predict halite precipitation patterns and their impact on permeability damage and energy recovery. Numerical results further show the model's value in predicting operational challenges such as wellbore blockage and the role of fracture connectivity. The model thus provides an open-source numerical tool for analysing complex heat and mass transport with mineral scaling in high-enthalpy fractured geothermal systems.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical model for salt precipitation and multiphase flow in fractured geothermal systems, focusing on reservoir engineering rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Simulating high-enthalpy fractured geothermal reservoirs is challenging due to complex coupled processes and mineral scaling that impairs permeability.
method: A compositional flow model with persistent primary variables (pressure, enthalpy, salt mass fraction) and a discrete fracture-matrix approach is implemented in the PorePy framework, using Kozeny-Carman relation for permeability reduction.
result: The model is verified against a benchmark and applied to a 2D fractured reservoir, showing capability to predict halite precipitation patterns and their impact on permeability and energy recovery.
conclusion: The model provides an open-source tool for analyzing heat and mass transport with mineral scaling in high-enthalpy fractured geothermal systems.

title: Local High Order Space-time Apdaptive Mlsdc
authors: Erik Pfister, Matti Schulze, J\"org Stiller
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building upon the semi-implicit multilevel spectral deferred correction (SI-MLSDC) method introduced by Pfister and Stiller [38], this work presents a 1D space-time adaptive high-order method combining discontinuous Galerkin spectral element discretizations with multilevel spectral deferred corrections. The proposed approach enables genuine arbitrary-order accuracy in space and time while dynamically balancing spatial and temporal discretization errors to reduce computational cost. A key contribution is the development of a novel temporal error estimator that in combination with a spectral error estimator in space provides a reliable basis for adaptive refinement decisions. The error estimator is compared with two alternative refinement criteria to assess their impact on accuracy, computational efficiency and their suitability for complex problems.The performance of the adaptive method is demonstrated for nonlinear conservation laws ranging from Burgers' equation to the Euler equations. Numerical results show substantial runtime reductions while maintaining the desired accuracy. In particular, significant computational savings are achieved for Burgers' equation, and challenging benchmark problems such as the Shu-Osher shock-fluctuation benchmark. These results demonstrate the potential of adaptive SI-MLSDC methods for efficient high-order space-time adaptive simulations of complex flow problems.
tldr: This paper presents a space-time adaptive high-order numerical method for solving conservation laws, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To improve computational efficiency of high-order simulations of complex flow problems by dynamically balancing spatial and temporal discretization errors.
method: Combines discontinuous Galerkin spectral element discretizations with multilevel spectral deferred corrections and introduces a novel temporal error estimator for adaptive refinement.
result: Demonstrates substantial runtime reductions while maintaining accuracy for nonlinear conservation laws including Burgers' equation and the Shu-Osher shock-fluctuation benchmark.
conclusion: The adaptive SI-MLSDC method is effective for efficient high-order space-time adaptive simulations of complex flow problems.

title: A Simulation Study On Spatial Exponential Decay Of Perturbations In A Two-dimensional Wave Equation With Optimal Boundary/line Control
authors: Benedikt Oppeneiger
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent results have shown that domain-uniform stabilizability and detectability imply spatial exponential decay of perturbations in optimally controlled hyperbolic PDEs on one-dimensional domains. This domain-uniform stabilizability and detectability can be achieved only if the control domain is distributed over the whole spatial domain such that the distance between neighboring control intervals is bounded from above. Motivated by these insights we investigate whether analogous effects can be observed for optimal boundary control in higher dimensions. For this purpose we conduct a simulation study on a two-dimensional wave equation on expanding square domains which is driven by a localized perturbation of the initial displacement. We compare two control geometries: a control acting only on the outer boundary and a control acting on a regular grid of interior line interfaces combined with the boundary. The problem is discretized by conforming P1 finite elements in space and the implicit midpoint rule in time. Instead of assembling the full space-time KKT system, we use a condensed formulation and solve the reduced optimality system by preconditioned conjugate gradients. We show that domain-uniform spatial decay of the perturbation can only be observed in the scenario with a regular grid of line controls. This is because finite propagation velocity requires a uniform bound on the distance that a wave can travel without reaching the control domain.
tldr: A simulation study on spatial exponential decay of perturbations in a 2D wave equation with optimal boundary/line control.
motivation: To investigate whether domain-uniform stabilizability and detectability imply spatial exponential decay of perturbations in higher-dimensional hyperbolic PDEs, as previously shown for 1D.
method: Discretizes the 2D wave equation using conforming P1 finite elements in space and implicit midpoint rule in time, solves the reduced optimality system via preconditioned conjugate gradients.
result: Spatial exponential decay of perturbations is observed only when a regular grid of line controls is used, not with boundary-only control, due to finite propagation velocity.
conclusion: Domain-uniform spatial decay requires a uniform bound on the distance waves travel without reaching the control domain, analogous to the 1D case.

title: Diffeomorphism Groups Of Compact Locally Polyhedral Manifolds
authors: Johanna Jakob
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A locally polyhedral manifold [MATH] is a manifold which is locally diffeomorph to open subsets of convex polytopes. Manifolds with corners are a special case of locally polyhedral manifolds. We turn the group [MATH] of all smooth diffeomorphisms [MATH] for compact smooth [MATH] into a regular Lie group.
tldr: This paper studies diffeomorphism groups of locally polyhedral manifolds, a topic in differential geometry and topology.
motivation: To understand the structure of diffeomorphism groups on manifolds with corners and more general locally polyhedral manifolds.
method: The author constructs a regular Lie group structure on the diffeomorphism group of a compact smooth locally polyhedral manifold.
result: The group of smooth diffeomorphisms of a compact smooth locally polyhedral manifold is a regular Lie group.
conclusion: This work extends the theory of diffeomorphism groups to a broader class of manifolds, with potential applications in geometry and analysis.

title: Shadowing In Dynamical Systems: Zero-dimensional Extensions And Inverse Limits
authors: Dekui Peng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Good and Meddaugh proved that every compact metric dynamical system with shadowing is a factor of the inverse limit of an inverse sequence of shifts of finite type. We show first that, for this factor representation alone, both assumptions are unnecessary: every compact Hausdorff dynamical system is a factor of the inverse limit of an inverse system of shifts of finite type. In particular, the mere existence of such a symbolic inverse-limit representation is not specific to shadowing. The main contribution of the paper is to identify the additional stability which shadowing provides in the metric case. We prove that every compact metric system with shadowing is a factor of the inverse limit of an inverse sequence of shifts of finite type whose bonding maps are surjective. Hence the inverse sequence satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition, and the corresponding zero-dimensional extension still has shadowing. This strengthens the metric representation theorem of Good and Meddaugh and completes their characterization in terms of ALP factors of Mittag-Leffler inverse sequences of shifts of finite type. Finally, for arbitrary compact Hausdorff spaces, we show that every compact shadowing system is conjugate to the inverse limit of metrizable shadowing systems with factor bonding maps. In this sense, compact shadowing systems are generated from shifts of finite type by applying, at most three times, the two shadowing-preserving operations of taking Mittag-Leffler inverse limits and passing to ALP factors.
tldr: This paper studies shadowing in dynamical systems and symbolic inverse-limit representations, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to generalize and strengthen a representation theorem for dynamical systems with shadowing, showing that shadowing is not necessary for such representations and identifying the additional structure shadowing provides.
method: The paper uses topological dynamics and inverse limit constructions, proving that every compact Hausdorff system is a factor of an inverse limit of shifts of finite type, and that metric shadowing systems correspond to Mittag-Leffler inverse sequences.
result: The main result is that every compact metric system with shadowing is a factor of an inverse limit of shifts of finite type with surjective bonding maps, and that compact shadowing systems are generated from shifts of finite type by three operations.
conclusion: The work completes the characterization of shadowing systems in terms of inverse limits of shifts of finite type, but has no relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Generalized Framework For A Fair Comparison Of Cellular And Cooperative Massive Mimo Systems
authors: Leonard Paul Schulz, Stefan Schwarz, Gerhard Bauch
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cooperative massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) promises large gains over cellular deployments, but existing comparisons of different architectures often mix antenna distribution, inter-site coordination, and processing assumptions. This paper introduces a graph-based framework for fair comparison of cellular, coordinated, and cell-free massive-MIMO systems. We differentiate between two key properties, namely antenna distribution and inter-site cooperation, which yields seven representative system types. We derive compatible uplink and downlink spectral efficiency (SE) expressions, including an uplink bound for detectors with mixed instantaneous and statistical effective channel state information (CSI), and adapt scalable user association and processing rules to all considered architectures. We evaluate these systems using extensive numerical simulations and show that for a fair comparison much larger simulation areas (at least 2.5 [MATH] 2.5 km2) than commonly used are required. We introduce the relative capacity, which measures how closely each architecture approaches centralized cell-free processing. The results show that coordinated, phase-aligned beamforming across spatially distributed antennas is the main source of cooperation gains. In dense deployments with few antennas per access point (AP), coordinated Distributed Antenna System (DAS) and hybrid cell-free architectures achieve much of the centralized cell-free performance while requiring substantially weaker midhaul assumptions.
tldr: This paper presents a graph-based framework for fair comparison of cellular, coordinated, and cell-free massive MIMO systems, focusing on spectral efficiency and antenna distribution.
motivation: Existing comparisons of massive MIMO architectures mix antenna distribution, coordination, and processing assumptions, leading to unfair evaluations.
method: The authors introduce a graph-based framework differentiating antenna distribution and inter-site cooperation, derive spectral efficiency expressions, and perform numerical simulations over large areas.
result: Coordinated phase-aligned beamforming across spatially distributed antennas is the main source of cooperation gains; hybrid architectures approach centralized cell-free performance with weaker midhaul requirements.
conclusion: The framework enables fair comparison and shows that coordinated distributed antenna systems achieve much of the centralized cell-free performance.

title: A Closed-form Convergence Criterion For The Weak Greedy Algorithm
authors: Mikhail Novikov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2002, V. N. Temlyakov established a criterion for the convergence of the weak greedy algorithm in a Hilbert space for a given weakness sequence [MATH]. The criterion requires verifying a certain limiting relation for every nonnegative square-summable sequence. method: The author derives an equivalent closed-form condition using mathematical analysis and properties of Hilbert spaces.
result: A necessary and sufficient condition for convergence of the weak greedy algorithm is given in closed form.
conclusion: The new criterion is easier to verify and provides deeper insight into the convergence behavior of the algorithm.

title: Nonlinear Two-Time-Scale Stochastic Approximation: A Sharp Phase Transition And How To Beat It
authors: Vaneet Aggarwal Dhruv Sarkar

title: Efficient And Fast Tensor-Product Multinode Shepard Collocation For Elliptic PDEs On Cartesian Grids
authors: Anouar El Harrak, Hatim Tayeq, Benaissa Zerroudi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a Grid-Based Multinode Shepard Collocation Method (GBMSC) for two-dimensional elliptic boundary value problems on rectangular domains. The method combines Shepard-type partition functions with tensor-product Lagrange interpolation on overlapping local Cartesian subgrids. The Cartesian structure avoids the local unisolvency search required by multinode Shepard constructions on scattered data, while the local character of the approximation yields sparse collocation matrices and moderate conditioning. We establish the main structural properties of the method, including the cardinal property, tensor-product polynomial reproduction, and local interpolation estimates. Numerical experiments for Poisson problems with Dirichlet and mixed boundary conditions confirm the polynomial reproduction property up to round-off accuracy and show regular convergence for smooth non-polynomial solutions. Comparisons with Multinode Shepard Collocation Method (MSC) and Kansa's collocation methods indicate that the proposed discretization preserves high accuracy with significantly better conditioning than the RBF-based schemes considered.
tldr: A numerical method for solving elliptic PDEs using tensor-product Shepard interpolation on Cartesian grids.
motivation: To develop an efficient and well-conditioned collocation method for elliptic PDEs that avoids the unisolvency issues of scattered-data Shepard methods.
method: Combines Shepard partition functions with tensor-product Lagrange interpolation on overlapping local Cartesian subgrids, yielding sparse collocation matrices.
result: The method achieves polynomial reproduction up to round-off accuracy and shows regular convergence for smooth solutions, with better conditioning than RBF-based methods.
conclusion: The proposed GBMSC method is a viable alternative for elliptic PDEs on rectangular domains, offering high accuracy and improved conditioning.

title: Nonparametric Inference On Fokker-Plank And McKean-Vlasov Models
authors: Roberto Imbuzeiro Oliveira Adriana Laurindo Monteiro
abstract: ArXiv:2606.14514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a kernel-based estimator of the velocity field governing the transport and diffusion of [MATH]-dimensional interacting particles. Assuming the initial positions are i.i.d. with law [MATH], we establish consistency of the estimator with an explicit mean-squared error rate of order [MATH], where [MATH] denotes the time-discretization step and N the number of particles. The analysis covers two distinct settings: the Fokker-Planck equation, where we recover the underlying potential function, and the McKean-Vlasov equation, where we deconvolve the interaction kernel driving the mean-field dynamics.
tldr: This paper proposes a kernel-based estimator for the velocity field in Fokker-Planck and McKean-Vlasov models, focusing on nonparametric inference for interacting particle systems.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of interacting particle systems is important in many fields, but existing methods may not be efficient or consistent for high-dimensional settings.
